text: As Putnam discusses in Bowling Alone. <break time="0.8s" /> There has been a notable decline. <break time="0.8s" /> In face to face social interactions. <break time="0.8s" /> Leading to an erosion of social capital. <break time="0.8s" /> Most famously. <break time="0.8s" /> As reflected in his books title. <break time="0.8s" /> Putnam pointed to the decline in bowling leagues. <break time="0.8s" /> As a metaphor for social disengagement. <break time="0.8s" /> While more people were bowling than ever before league bowling dropped by 40 percent. <break time="0.8s" /> From 1970 to 1993. <break time="0.8s" /> His research depicts a society. <break time="0.8s" /> That has lost many foundational opportunities for communal bonding. <break time="0.8s" /> Giving rise to an era marked by isolation and detachment. <break time="0.8s" /> He connected the dissolution of civic organizations like Lions Clubs. <break time="0.8s" /> And social groups like bowling leagues. <break time="0.8s" /> With the drop in social trust among Americans. <break time="0.8s" /> And warned of the negative impact it has on our individual and collective lives. <break time="0.8s" /> He wrote. <break time="0.8s" /> The single most common finding. <break time="0.8s" /> From a half centurys research on the correlates of life satisfaction. <break time="0.8s" /> Not only in the United States but around the world. <break time="0.8s" /> Is that happiness is best predicted. <break time="0.8s" /> By the breadth and depth of ones social connections.
